subject: Clarify 'commit insurance' smoothing clause in order schedule - annex attached
messages:
From: James Lowe <j.lowe@acmehealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Miller <hmiller@bluerocklaw.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Question on 'commit insurance' smoothing clause in order schedule
Attachments: Acme_Order_Schedule_v3.xlsx

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the updated order schedule. Our procurement team flagged the new 'commit insurance' smoothing language in Exhibit B — they want clarity on how the smoothing operates against the minimum monthly floors and whether the escrow calculation can cause a retrospective charge. Two quick asks: (1) can you confirm if smoothing applies only to billed usage (post-invoice) or to committed units reported for true-up? (2) what specific triggers would cause Redwood to draw from the escrow/insurance bucket?

I've attached the schedule we received; Hannah (Acme counsel) is cc'd and will loop in legal redlines. Would prefer to resolve this without a formal SOW amendment if possible.

- James
James Lowe
Head of Procurement, AcmeHealth
procurement@acmehealth.com

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: James Lowe <j.lowe@acmehealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Oct 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question on 'commit insurance' smoothing clause in order schedule
Attachments: Exhibit_B_Pricing_Annex_redline.docx (staged)

Hi James — thanks for the note and for surfacing Acme's procurement concerns. Quick answers up front:
- Smoothing (our intent) applies to invoiced usage windows; it is forward-looking and designed to reduce volatility in billing over the quarter rather than produce a retroactive draw that creates unexpected one-off charges.
- Escrow/insurance draws are intended to cover shortfalls relative to the committed baseline after a defined true-up window (60 days after quarter close) and only when a floor breach persists beyond the cure period. They are not used as an immediate debit on an invoice.

That said, I recognize the language in v3 is ambiguous. I'm attaching a proposed redline of Exhibit B that: (a) adds a short waterfall of triggers (60/90/120-day cure steps), (b) clarifies that smoothing reconciliations are reflected on the next invoice cycle (not retroactive), and (c) caps escrow draws to the quarterly average of committed units, not total historical usage.

Laura / Ben — can you review the attached redline and confirm if we can accept the quarter-average cap and the 60/90/120 cure steps? If legal or finance wants different gating (e.g., monetary cap vs. unit cap) call it out here and I'll push back to Acme.

If this looks acceptable to Acme, I'd prefer to incorporate the redline as an annex to the order schedule and avoid reopening the main MSA.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
(650) 555-0178

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Oct 2027 13:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question on 'commit insurance' smoothing clause in order schedule

On Tue, Oct 12, 2027 at 10:05 AM karthik_iyer@redwood.com wrote:
> I'm attaching a proposed redline of Exhibit B that: (a) adds a short waterfall of triggers (60/90/120-day cure steps), (b) clarifies that smoothing reconciliations are reflected on the next invoice cycle (not retroactive), and (c) caps escrow draws to the quarterly average of committed units, not total historical usage.

Karthik — thanks. From a legal perspective:
- Prefer the unit-based cap (quarterly average) over a pure monetary cap; it ties back to capacity planning and is easier to audit.
- Suggest tightening the cure windows to 45/75/105 days to reduce lingering exposure; Acme's ask to avoid retroactive charges is reasonable — keep the "no retroactive debit" sentence.
- Add explicit language that any draw from escrow requires a single-signature approval from Redwood Finance and a notification to Acme with an itemized calculation.

I'll prepare a clean markup that reflects the 45/75/105 schedule and the approval/notify step. Ben — please flag any commercial objections to the approval requirement (it will add an ops step).

Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Oct 2027 13:50:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question on 'commit insurance' smoothing clause in order schedule

Agree with Laura's edits except one commercial point: if we move to 45/75/105 days it tightens our remediation playbook and increases operational churn. Compromise: keep the 60/90/120 but add an optional early-termination trigger where either side can request accelerated reconciliation in writing (mutual consent) — this preserves our ops cadence while giving Acme a path to a faster resolution if they prefer.

Also recommend we preserve an "escrow floor" equal to 10% of the quarterly committed units to prevent gaming small flares. That should be acceptable to both sides and avoids frequent small draws.

Ben Carter
VP, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

From: Hannah Miller <hmiller@bluerocklaw.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, James Lowe <j.lowe@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Oct 2027 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Acme redline: Exhibit B — commit insurance / smoothing (vAcme_annotated)
Attachments: Acme_ExhibitB_redline.pdf

Karthik / James —

Thanks for the context. We've reviewed Redwood's v3 schedule and attached our annotated Exhibit B. Topline from Acme legal:
- We cannot accept any language that permits escrow draws without a documented default event; please replace "cure steps" with a clear definition of "Material Under-commitment Event" (e.g., >25% shortfall vs. committed baseline for two consecutive months).
- We prefer a monetary cap on draws (3x average monthly commitment) rather than a units-based cap so that our finance team can model liquidity.
- Request explicit carveout that smoothing adjustments cannot change historical SLA credit calculations (i.e., smoothing only affects billing, not SLA performance measurement).

I've attached the annotated PDF and included suggested phrasing. For negotiation, Acme wants the following: monetary cap + Material Under-commitment Event trigger + 90-day cure window.

We can do a short call to reconcile positions early next week — propose Mon 09:00 PT.

Hannah Miller
Counsel, BlueRock Legal (on behalf of AcmeHealth)
hmiller@bluerocklaw.com

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: James Lowe <j.lowe@acmehealth.com>, Hannah Miller <hmiller@bluerocklaw.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Oct 2027 16:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Acme redline: Exhibit B — commit insurance / smoothing (vAcme_annotated)
Attachments: Exhibit_B_Pricing_Annex_redline_v2.docx

Thanks Hannah — helpful and clear. Quick summary of where we land internally and suggested approach for the call:
- We can accept a monetary cap instead of a unit cap if we define the calculation as "3x average monthly committed USD value" (aligns to Ben's ops guardrails).
- Laura wants an explicit "default event" definition; Acme's proposed "Material Under-commitment Event" threshold (>25% shortfall x 2 months) is reasonable as long as we keep the optional early-termination/accelerated reconciliation pathway for mutual consent.
- Redwood will require that any escrow draw include a single Finance approval and a 10-business-day prior notification to Acme with an itemized calculation.

Proposed next steps:
1) I'll upload Exhibit_B_Pricing_Annex_redline_v2 (attaching) that swaps the unit cap to the monetary cap and adds the approval/notify step plus the mutual-consent early reconciliation language.
2) Schedule a 30-minute call Mon 09:00 PT to walk the markup and finalize the annex; if we converge we will execute the annex as a post-signature addendum to the order schedule (no MSA amendment).

James / Hannah — does Mon 09:00 PT work for you? If yes, I'll send a calendar invite and a short comparison slide showing the bounds of compromise.

Appreciate the collaboration — want to keep this tight and avoid reopening larger commercial terms.

Best,
Karthik
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
